named_events.event_name: fire on an offshore rig complex
named_events.loss_description: The largest loss ($9.5m net), was the result of a fire on an offshore rig complex and impacted the Energy and Marine XL classes.

Cargo & Specie returned a $4.4m underwriting profit, broadly breaking-even for the year having taken expenses into account and successfully withstanding another of the largest headline losses, the Tianjin Chinese port explosion.

It was a good year for the Hull and Terrorism accounts which recorded solid profits of $11.9m (2014: $15.9m profit) and $9.4m (2014: $16.1m profit) respectively and in particular for Terrorism which weathered its first losses of any significance, relating to the Yemeni civil war.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross strengthening of $23.366 million in prior year reserves, primarily due to adverse claims development across various underwriting years from 2008 to 2013. This is in contrast to a narrative statement of a net release of $6.284 million on claims outstanding from the previous year end. The strengthening is also influenced by late claims notifications in long-tail classes like Professional Indemnity.
raw_causal_phrases: a higher than expected number of risk losses advised in June
number of new large losses experienced in June in particular
positive and negative movements to the incurred claims position
one off late claims notifications rather than any systemic issues arising within the lines of business themselves
data.data_quality_notes: The narrative on page 30 states a net release of $6.284 million for prior year claims outstanding. However, the gross claims development triangle on page 41 indicates a gross strengthening of $23.366 million for prior underwriting years (2008-2013). The gross triangle figure is used as per instructions, with this discrepancy noted.
